packageChain.chainRepairNote: FORK REPAIRED. The Steps-1-72 and Steps-1-100 snapshots both declared PAF-RUN7A-CONTINUATION-v1.0 as predecessor, so the chain forked rather than extended and the 1-72 package was absent from the ancestry. This package chains correctly to PAF-STEPS-1-100-PACKAGE by its measured SHA-256. thisPackageId, previously stale at PAF-STEPS-1-100-PACKAGE while state had advanced well beyond it, is also corrected.
packageChain.packageIsThin: THIN PACKAGE — owner decision 2026-08-21 (option B). This package carries the continuity snapshot and a manifest pointing at the repository. It does NOT carry a copy of the governed corpus. The repository at the commit below is the system of record. Measured before this decision: of 158 files in the previous fat package, 141 were byte-identical to the repository, 7 differed with the repository newer in every case, and 3 were absent — two READMEs describing the package itself and its own checksum file. The fat package therefore carried no information the repository lacked, while going stale between every session. That staleness was recorded as R-03.
packageChain.whyNotRetiredEntirely: Retiring the mechanism was considered and rejected on evidence. paf.continuity-snapshot.schema.json lists packageChain as a REQUIRED field, and packageChain requires thisPackageId, immutableCorpusHash and predecessorPackageHash. Removing it would produce a snapshot failing its own frozen schema, enforced by validate_framework.py — which would require a governed change against the frozen core to remove a safety mechanism. Thin satisfies the schema honestly while removing the staleness.

defectsFound.defect: The database projectone_dev did not exist. sys.databases held only master, model, msdb and tempdb. Canonical Step 99 configured the local development database CONNECTION; nothing ever created the database itself.
defectsFound.symptom: pyodbc.InterfaceError reporting 'Login failed for user' — misleading. The operative error was 4060, 'Cannot open database projectone_dev requested by the login'. SQL Server reports a login failure when it cannot open the requested database, so the message points at authentication when the cause is a missing database.
defectsFound.fix: CREATE DATABASE projectone_dev — empty, no schema. Environment setup, not implementation; clear of the Step 112 gate.
defectsFound.latency: Latent since Step 99. Invisible until the connection was exercised end to end, because configuring a connection string never touches the server.

defectsFound.defect: The 999 overlay register created at canonical Step 108 claimed to supersede the external 999-Agent-Build-Canon-Modification-Tracker-v0.4.md while containing only OV-001 and OV-002. That tracker held 27 APPROVED entries. None had been migrated.
defectsFound.howItHappened: The register was authored without access to the external tracker. The gap WAS flagged at the time as NOT_EXAMINED in PR #11's evidence section, so it was not a silent miss — but the header's supersedes claim was written as though complete, and stood untrue for six days.
defectsFound.whyItMattered: A register that looks complete is more dangerous than one that is obviously partial. A reader checking 'are there overlays on the DDR?' would have found none and concluded correctly from a false premise.
defectsFound.fix: All 27 entries migrated verbatim with original approvals; supersedes claim corrected; register v1.0 -> v2.0.
defectsFound.foundBy: Owner. John directed a double-check of whether prior DDR change proposals had been evaluated.
defectsFound.lesson: A NOT_EXAMINED note protects honesty but does not protect the artifact. When a claim depends on something unexamined, weaken the CLAIM, do not merely footnote it.

carriedForward.subject: Version drift across Project-knowledge canonical documents
carriedForward.status: RESOLVED 2026-08-22 — already ruled on in the external tracker; ruling now migrated into the repository
carriedForward.severity: Material. These are Tier-1/Tier-2 canonical documents and they disagree with each other on paper.
findings: 402 Tracker: header reads v84; its own 'current canonical versions' line reads v82; the Manifest reads v80. Three values.
403 Manifest: header reads v73; its own inventory row for itself reads v49; the Tracker reads v70. Three values.

201 DDR: file header reads v1.35 while BOTH the Manifest and the Tracker claim v1.37. Either the header is stale after surgical edits, or the file itself is an older version. Nobody can tell which from inside the repository.
carriedForward.whyItMatters: The DDR is the design authority and wins every conflict. A design authority whose own version cannot be established is a weak foundation for the first vertical slice.
carriedForward.whereTheseLive: Claude Project knowledge and the Core Build Reference Package — NOT this repository. Some are immutable uploaded sources, so corrections may require 999 overlays rather than edits. See governance/overlays/PROJECTONE-999-Overlay-Register.json for the mechanism.
carriedForward.notDoneBecause: Out of scope for the 101-111 range, which governs the repository. Deliberately deferred, not forgotten.
carriedForward.recommendedTiming: Before or during Step 112, since F1a work reads from the DDR.
carriedForward.resolution: The drift was not an open question. AB-CM-029, approved by John 2026-08-11, states the current authoritative DDR is v1.37 and explicitly names v1.23, v1.26, v1.27, v1.29, v1.33 and v1.35 as superseded. The DDR file header reading v1.35 is therefore a STALE HEADER, not an older file — the exact ambiguity that could not be settled from inside the repository. AB-CM-030 does the same for the Manifest's DDR row, and AB-CM-016 and AB-CM-029 cover the Tracker's own pointers.
